items.note: 20 novices co-wrote cartoon captions with an NLP incongruity tool and 66 raters judged them funnier than captions written without the tool; full text must confirm the tool is generative AI and how the no-tool captions were produced.

Within-subjects study with 12 designers comparing a structured multi-phase prompt-based design tool with a conversational AI baseline (AI versus AI configuration); computed prompt and image diversity outcomes; well below 50 participants.

Randomized LLM-use policy for ICML 2026 reviewers (subset of 17,000 reviewers) with outcomes on paper decisions, scores, confidence and review length; peer review is not a creative task and no creativity or diversity outcome is scored.

Within-subject study comparing the Reverger AI story-ideation tool with a comparable baseline; participants explored more unexpected and diverse directions; sample size and whether the baseline uses AI are not stated in the abstract.

Comparative study (N=24) of AtoMix, a generative-image 6-3-5 brainwriting interface, against a baseline (likely a GenAI interface); formative study N=18 reported redundancy and limited divergence; unclear whether idea diversity is scored.

User study with 10 fashion designers comparing the CLAY text-to-image tool with their existing practice; outcomes (design time, expanded creative possibilities) look largely self-reported, so this may be self_report_only or system_paper_no_comparison on full-text reading.

System paper for Amuse, a multimodal-LLM chord-suggestion tool, with a user study of songwriters; the abstract names no comparison condition and the creativity outcome looks self-reported, so it may be out (system_paper_no_comparison) after full-text check.

Within-subject study with 16 professional UX designers doing one UI task with FigmaAI and one without; AI-assisted designs were more visually and structurally similar; task-order randomization not stated.

Book chapter (arXiv 2512.00010) comparing ideation sessions assisted by the ALIA analogical LLM agent with traditional sessions; preliminary results rest on participants' self-ratings; likely an earlier report of the same tool and possibly the same sample as c816.

Controlled ideation experiments with 24 undergraduate design students, where groups with an LLM analogical-stimuli tool (ALIA) produced higher-rated ideas than unassisted groups; also benchmarks LLMs; related to c815.
